messages:
anya: heads up — CI evals started failing on quantized bring-up for m-7b-q8, looks like a shard distribution thing rather than the model itself
anya: failing tests are the synthetic prompt-split goldenruns, mostly on runner shards 2 and 3
samir: ugh, saw a couple of those in the pipeline dashboard. any obvious diffs in the fixture ordering?
anya: ordering looks stable locally, but when the quantized runner is used the prompt augmentation step sometimes pushes a sample into the next shard 
samir: interesting. could be the tokenization length change with q8 artifacts affecting prefix grouping
matt: can you paste the failing lines from the runner log?
anya: sure, here's the chunk that recurs in CI logs:
```
[2024-07-22T14:12:03Z] runner: initializing shard=3 total_shards=8 seed=42
[2024-07-22T14:12:03Z] runner: loading fixtures: promptset_v12_syn_aug.json (N=12,345)
[2024-07-22T14:12:03Z] augment: applied length-trim -> new_len=64 orig_len=128 sample_id=9802
[2024-07-22T14:12:03Z] shard_assign: hash(sample_id, seed)=981523 -> assigned_shard=4
[2024-07-22T14:12:03Z] error: expected shard=3 but got assigned_shard=4 for sample 9802
```
leah: that pattern matches our earlier 'post-augment hashing' problem — we used to compute shard assignment before augmentation and recently flipped to after to improve balance for long sequences
leah: flipping the order was intentional for hosted throughput but it will make CI goldenruns non-deterministic compared to the stored fixtures
samir: ah, so quantization changes tokenization -> augmentation modifies length -> assignment flips -> goldenrun diffs. makes sense
anya: wanted to check whether to (A) revert ordering in eval harness for goldenruns only, (B) make shard assignment use stable sample ids pre-augment, or (C) update fixtures to be post-augment snapshot
matt: (B) seems safest for CI determinism — use original sample_id or stable fingerprint before any augmentation/length changes. then runtime can remap for production.
leah: agreed. small PR: eval-runner will compute fingerprint = sha1(sample_text + seed) at fixture load time and use that for shard assignment, then apply augmentation. keeps golden run stable
samir: does that risk reintroducing imbalance when running distributed smoke runs? we might see hot shards if augmentation radically changes token lengths
leah: we can keep current dynamic assignment for perf runs, add a flag `--stable-shard-assignment` that the CI goldenrun config sets to true
anya: perfect. can somebody open a tiny PR and add the flag to the CI job config and the runner defaults?
matt: I'll do it. PR will include unit test: run 10k synthetic samples with and w/o stable assignment and assert deterministic mapping for the same seed across runs
matt: also adding a regression test that mirrors the log snippet above to ensure we don't silently flip in CI
ci-bot: created ticket #ENG-ML-762: add stable-shard-assignment flag + CI job change. linked PR draft matt/eng-ml/runner#128
anya: thanks — once PR is up I'll re-run the failing goldenruns and confirm
leah: FYI we should also add a note to the docs about augmentation order and determinism, small blurb under eval-harness/fixtures.md
samir: good call. can we also add a terse metric in console: "shard-consistency-ratio" for goldenruns so we catch regressions earlier?
leah: yes, I'll add it to the rollup dashboard (per-promptset metric)
anya: thanks team, this explains the weird CI-only regressions we've been chasing. will re-run after PR lands and follow up with results here :thumbsup:
